subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps - Aurora Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Stacey Williams <stacey.williams@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps - Aurora Health

Stacey — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of needs / pain:
- Sensitive PHI processing for clinical summarization and triage; must meet HIPAA and Aurora internal audit controls.
- Current latency and cost issues with self-hosted endpoints; spikes during morning batch ingestion cause timeouts.
- Need isolation (single-tenant) and guaranteed throughput for peak windows.

Customer goals:
- Deploy a private/dedicated inference pool (no multi-tenant sharing) with strict network isolation and KMS integration.
- Target p95 response latency <= 200ms for common prompt sizes; SLA requirement 99.9% uptime.
- Predictable per-month cost and the ability to scale reserved GPUs during growth.

Initial sizing discussed (ballpark):
- Reserved capacity: 8x A100 40GB-equivalent GPUs dedicated to Aurora traffic (can propose alternative GPU mixes after sizing).
- Autoscale inset/overflow policy for short bursts up to 12x with burst credits.
- KV/prefix caching for repeated clinical prompts; model quantization options to reduce token cost.

Open questions we need from you to finalize sizing:
1) Typical request concurrency and average output token length for the models you plan to serve (estimates are fine).
2) Required cloud region (you mentioned US East) and any data residency constraints.
3) Timeline for procurement / PO and if there are any required contract terms beyond standard Redwood EULA.

Attachments: preliminary quote and draft SLA for Aurora (redwood-dedicated-quote-AH.pdf, aurora-sla-draft.docx).

Proposed next steps:
- I'll loop in Vivek (cc'd) for a technical sizing call — he can validate GPU mix and autoscaling parameters.
- Rafael will follow up with a formal quote and sample contract redlines.
- If agreeable, we can provision a capacity hold for 30 days while procurement completes.

Available times for the technical call this week: Wed 10–12 PDT, Thu 14–17 PDT, Fri 9–11 PDT.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Stacey Williams <stacey.williams@aurorahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aurora Procurement <procurement@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps - Aurora Health

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap, this matches our notes. A few clarifications and answers to your questions:

1) Concurrency / tokens: our initial workload will be ~150–200 concurrent sessions during peak; average model output is ~800 tokens, average input ~200 tokens. We expect sustained peak windows of ~45–90 minutes in the morning and another shorter spike midday.
2) Region: must be hosted in US East (us-east-1) for data residency.
3) Compliance: HIPAA-eligible deployment required; we will need KMS/HSM integration, audit logs retention for 1 year, and SOC2 evidence.
4) Procurement timeline: procurement estimates 4–6 weeks once we have a final SOW and quote. They also requested a standard BAAs template; procurement@aurorahealth.com is the contact for contracts.

Can you confirm the isolation model will be single-tenant with VPC peering and that logs/evidence can be delivered for audits? Also please confirm cost impact if we move from 8x A100 to a mixed fleet (e.g., 4x A100 + 8x A10) — we may prefer a cost-conservative mix if performance still meets latency targets.

Happy to do the technical sizing call. Wed 11am PDT works for us.

Thanks,
Stacey
Director, Clinical AI | Aurora Health
stacey.williams@aurorahealth.com | +1 212-555-0199

Date: 2026-06-11T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps - Aurora Health

Stacey — great, thanks for the clarity and for confirming Wed 11am PDT. Quick replies inline and next actions.

- Isolation / architecture: yes — we will provision a single-tenant dedicated pool for Aurora with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. Audit logs and retention for 12 months can be provided; I'll have our security team attach the SOC2 artifact.
- Region: we will size in us-east-1 per your requirement.
- Mixed fleet: Vivek will run a perf/price matrix (4x A100 + 8x A10 vs 8x A100) and recommend the best cost/perf tradeoff to meet p95 <= 200ms for your typical prompt sizes.

Attached is a refined preliminary quote (redwood-dedicated-quote-AH.pdf) and the draft SLA (aurora-sla-draft.docx) with the 99.9% uptime target. Rafael has included sample pricing for a 12-month reserved term and optional burst credits.

Proposed immediate next steps (action items):
1) Technical sizing call — Wed 2026-06-12 11:00am PDT (Vivek will send a calendar invite).
2) Redwood to deliver a final sizing report and updated quote within 3 business days of the call.
3) Aurora to confirm procurement timeline and send PO contact details to Rafael.

Rafael — can you please prepare the PO-ready quote PDF and include standard BAAs terms for Aurora procurement? Vivek — please prepare perf/price options (A100-only vs mixed fleet) and recommended autoscale headroom.

If there are no major redlines to the SLA, we can hold the proposed capacity for 30 days while procurement works on the PO.

Thanks — see you on Wed.

—
